title: On the Role of Speech Data in Reducing Toxicity Detection Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the false positive rate (FPR) of speech- and text-based toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples mentioning specific gender identities (e.g., female, male, transgender).
Comparing the false positive rate (FPR) of speech- and text-based toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples mentioning specific racial or ethnic groups (e.g., Black, White, etc.).
Comparing the false positive rate (FPR) of speech- and text-based toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples mentioning specific religious groups (e.g., Muslim, Christian).
Evaluating the false positive rate (FPR) of toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples annotated for mentions of sexual orientations (e.g., homosexual, gay, lesbian, bisexual).

Evaluating the false positive rate (FPR) of toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples annotated for mentions of social classes or socio-economic statuses (e.g., poverty, working class, upper class).
Evaluating the false positive rate (FPR) of toxicity detection classifiers on audio and text samples annotated for mentions of disabilities.
